Article Title: 'Plotting a super-tainted majority': Congress taunts Centre over delay in Parliament prorogation
Article Text:
File photo: Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Congress on Friday mounted its attack against the centre over the delay in prorogation of Parliament after it adjourned sine die, accusing the government of plotting a "super tainted two-third majority" to get the Delimitation Bill passed in Lok Sabha.In a social media post on X, Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said the gap between the adjournment of Parliament sine die and its prorogation has reached 29 days."So today the Modi govt has set a new record, bettering its own set in 2015. The gap between the adjournment of Parliament sine die and its prorogation has reached 29 days. The gap for the 2015 Monsoon Session was 28 days. The gap for the 2026 Monsoon Session is increasing by the day with no clear prospect for its early prorogation. Normally the gap is just three-four days," Jairam Ramesh said."It is abundantly clear that the Union home minister was severely wounded by the stunning defeat he had inflicted on himself and his govt with his staggering arrogance in the Lok Sabha on April 17, 2026. He is now plotting a comeback to secure a super-tainted two-thirds majority to get the Constitution Amendment Bill passed in the Lok Sabha. He has already engineered a split in three parties that had voted against the Bill on April 17, 2026, and is using threats, intimidation and incentives to get others (who had also voted against the Bill) to change their stance.The Union home minister does not have the numbers but his bravado, bluff and bluster will not let him read the writing on the wall," he added.The Congress leader said that the government is keeping the suspense going, thinking that the opposition will get rattled."By not proroguing the Monsoon Session, the self-styled Chanakya may think he is playing mind games and indulging in psy-ops. But this is silly since the govt can convene a session any time it wants to for any purpose. He is just keeping the suspense going, thinking that the opposition will get rattled. He can continue to hallucinate," Jairam Ramesh said."Why is the Modi govt refusing to convene an All-Party meeting to discuss its proposals for delimitation so as to build the broadest possible consensus - which is what the country needs? This has been the consistent demand of all opposition Parties since mid-March 2026. Why this secrecy and mystery on a subject that is of profound importance to the very fundamentals of the Indian Republic?" he questioned.This comes as Congress has been questioning the delay in proroguing Parliament's Monsoon session, saying "something fishy" was going on and the government was trying to conjure up a "super-tainted" two-thirds majority, but it would not succeed in achieving that.During the Budget session on April 17, the Modi government faced a setback as the Constitution amendment bill, involving delimitation, for the implementation of the women's reservation in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies was defeated in the Lower House.Of the 528 MPs who voted, 298 voted in support, while 230 opposed it. The bill required 352 votes for a two-thirds majority.
Article Summary: The gap between the adjournment of Parliament sine die and its prorogation has reached 29 days. The gap for the 2015 Monsoon Session was 28 days. Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said the government is keeping the suspense going, thinking the opposition will get rattled.

Article Title: 'Prioritise national interest': Shashi Tharoor advises govt to keep Brics 'non-West'
Article Text:
Shashi Tharoor says govt must keep Brics non-West and not let it appear anti-West.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Shashi Tharoor on Friday cautioned that the Brics summit hosted by India should not appear to be an anti-West platform, as that would not be in sync with the country’s national interests.Tharoor, who served as a diplomat at the United Nations for decades, advised the government to showcase the concerns of the Global South while keeping India’s direct national interests in mind."As chair, we have a particular responsibility to showcase both the Brics as a forum, the concerns of the Global South in general, but also while bearing very, very carefully in mind our direct national interests. We want Brics to be a forum that is non-West, but not anti-West. That is exactly actually the same agenda as every other country. There are some others in Brics who are very happy to take it as a geopolitical non-Western, but also anti-Western platform," Tharoor told news agency PTI.He also said that PM Modi's scheduled meeting with Chinese president Xi Jinping and the meeting with Russian president Vladimir Putin "are going to grab world headlines"."And I would like to say that that would not be in India's national interest...Becauseall these world leaders are in India, there will be significant bilateral conversations. Our Prime Minister is bound to be meeting each of the visiting heads of state and government who seeks a meeting. And that may mean a dozen important meetings with these country leaders. And for us, of course, both the meeting with President Xi and the meeting with President Putin are going to grab world headlines," the Thiruvananthapuram Lok Sabha MP said.Former Union minister Salman Khurshid also described the gathering as a “significant event” that allows India to demonstrate leadership on the global stage.Speaking to ANI, Khurshid stressed that the presence of leaders from all 11 member countries, including China, Iran, Russia, South Africa and India, could help New Delhi bring countries together, reduce contradictions and conflicts, and work towards creating better conditions in the world."This is a significant event. We hosted the G20 summit a few years ago, and the important thing is that the top leadership of China, Iran, Russia, South Africa, and India will all be present. All 11 countries will be present. It allows India to demonstrate leadership and ensure that contradictions and conflicts are reduced to a minimum. It can't be done overnight, but at least some attempt should be made. For India to have a locus as the leader and chairperson of the Brics summit, to be able to bring people together, converge, and accept positions that will create better conditions in the world," he said.Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday said leaders from across the world would gather in New Delhi over the next few days for the Brics summit, expressing confidence that the high-level meeting would see positive and meaningful discussions on various issues with the welfare of the world in mind.“Over the next few days, leaders from around the world will gather for the Brics Summit. I am confident that the Summit will see positive and meaningful discussions on various issues with the welfare of the world in mind,” Modi said in a post on X in Hindi.The Prime Minister also shared a Sanskrit shlok highlighting the importance of cultivating relationships with virtuous people and promoting dialogue and goodwill.“A person should always live among the virtuous and cultivate their company. A person should engage in discussion and foster friendly relations with the virtuous, because mutual goodwill, dialogue and friendly relations strengthen peace and cooperation,” the verse said in a loose translation.As Brics chair in 2026, India will host the 18th Brics summit in New Delhi on September 12 and 13. The summit will bring together leaders of Brics member and partner countries, as well as outreach invitees.During the summit, leaders are expected to discuss ways to strengthen intra-Brics cooperation on common priorities and exchange views on global and regional issues of mutual importance, according to a statement issued by the Ministry of External Affairs.Earlier on Thursday night, Bharat Mandapam, the venue for the summit in New Delhi, was being readied to host the high-profile gathering, with leaders and representatives from across the world expected to arrive for the September 12-13 event.
Article Summary: Shashi Tharoor says govt must keep Brics non-West and not let it appear anti- West. PM Modi's scheduled meeting with Chinese president Xi Jinping and the meeting with Russian president Vladimir Putin "are going to grab world headlines"

Article Title: Yogi Adityanath pays tribute to UP's first CM Govind Ballabh Pant on his 139th birth anniversary
Article Text:
Yogi Adityanath pays tribute to UP's first CM Govind Ballabh Pant on his 139th birth anniversary

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Thursday paid floral tribute to the state's first chief minister and freedom fighter Pandit Govind Ballabh Pant on his 139th birth anniversary, recalling his contributions to India's freedom struggle, governance and social reforms.Speaking at an event held to mark the birth anniversary, Yogi Adityanath described Pant as a great advocate and freedom fighter who played a significant role in the country's struggle for independence."On this occasion, on behalf of the Government of Uttar Pradesh and the revered people of Uttar Pradesh, I pay homage to the memories of Pandit Govind Ballabh Pant ji on the occasion of his auspicious birth anniversary, and offer my humble tributes," Yogi said.Recalling Pant's contribution to the Kakori case, the chief minister said that in 1925, Pant had strongly defended revolutionaries facing a case filed by the British government following the Kakori Train Action.He said Pant actively participated in the freedom movement and resigned as the Premier of Uttar Pradesh after being elected to the post in 1937, choosing instead to join the struggle against British rule."Whether it was the Quit India Movement or other major agitations from time to time for the freedom struggle, he actively took part in them," Yogi said.The Chief Minister highlighted Pant's role after Independence, saying he became the first chief minister of Uttar Pradesh in 1947, when present-day Uttarakhand was also part of the state."As the first chief minister of Uttar Pradesh... he initiated efforts to present the governance of such a large state as a model of good governance, foster its economic development, and work for the welfare of every section of society," he said.Yogi also recalled Pant's contribution to land reforms and described the model introduced during his tenure as exemplary.Later, as Union Home minister from 1954, Pant worked to address linguistic conflicts and played an important role in establishing Hindi as the official language, Yogi said."On this occasion, on behalf of the Government of Uttar Pradesh and the people of Uttar Pradesh, I pay homage to his memory and offer my humble tributes to him," the chief minister said.
Article Summary: Yogi Adityanath pays tribute to UP's first CM Govind Ballabh Pant on his 139th birth anniversary. Yogi described Pant as a great advocate and freedom fighter who played a significant role in the country's struggle for independence.

Article Title: "Legacy of our ancestors...": CM Pushkar Singh Dhami hails Rudrapur's transformative growth at Punjabi Gaurav Sammelan
Article Text:
"Legacy of our ancestors...": CM Pushkar Singh Dhami hails Rudrapur's transformative growth at Punjabi Gaurav Sammelan

Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Thursday lauded the pioneering legacy and transformative contributions of the ancestors and various communities in turning Rudrapur into a vibrant industrial hub and the granary of the nation.Speaking at the Punjabi Gaurav Sammelan in Rudrapur, the chief minister expressed deep gratitude to the Sikh Gurus for the ancestral sacrifices that laid the groundwork for the state's progress."I bow in reverence at the feet of all our Gurus. I pray to the Guru Sahibs that the spirit of service towards our society and our state remains alive within all of us," he said.CM Dhami hailed the development done in Rudrapur, highlighting that this is the same region that once faced threats of venomous snakes and scorpions and deadly animals like crocodiles and tigers."Look at the wonderful work being done here; may we all continue to receive the strength to undertake such noble tasks. Every community is progressing. There was a time when people spoke of the dangers here: snakes, scorpions, massive crocodiles, tigers. Yet, it was settled and transformed into what it is today, a hub of industry and a land of lush green fields that serve as a granary, supplying food to the entire nation.This is the legacy of our ancestors; we must cherish and preserve it," he said.Meanwhile, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) national president Nitin Nabin, who was also present at the programme as part of his two-day visit to the State, highlighted the Centre's interventions to protect persecuted minority communities from neighbouring nations, specifically referencing the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA).Nabin said, "We all know how there was a threat to the existence of the Sikh community in Afghanistan. A law that should have been made in the initial years of independence took a long time to be formed."Further, Nabin emphasised that the Modi government fulfilled a long-standing post-independence commitment by offering refuge and dignity to persecuted Sikhs and Hindus."With CAA (Citizenship Amendment Act), PM Narendra Modi fulfilled the promise that was made to people at the time of independence. Sikhs and Hindus who were facing atrocities in Pakistan, Afghanistan and Bangladesh are welcomed here not as refugees but as the children of this soil," he said.Earlier today, Nitin Nabin and Pushkar Singh Dhami paid floral tributes at the Shaheed Smarak in Haldwin honour of soldiers who laid down their lives for the nation.Nabin, along with CM Dhami, also offered prayers and performed rituals at the Mahalaxmi Temple in Haldwani earlier in the day. (ANI)
Article Summary: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Thursday lauded the pioneering legacy and transformative contributions of the ancestors and various communities. He expressed deep gratitude to the Sikh Gurus for the ancestral sacrifices that laid the groundwork for the state's progress. Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) national president Nitin Nabin highlighted the Centre's interventions to protect persecuted minority communities.

Article Title: BJP national president Nitin Nabin, Uttarakhand CM Pushkar Singh Dhami interact with youth in Haldwani
Article Text:
Uttarakhand CM Pushkar Singh Dhami and BJP national president Nitin Nabin interact with youth in Haldwani, Uttarakhand, on September 20, 2026.

Nabin cites central schemes, emerging opportunities

Dhami highlights recruitment, self-employment

Sports infrastructure, technology and investment

HALDWANI: BJP national president Nitin Nabin and Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami took part in a youth interaction programme in Haldwani, where they discussed careers, employment, entrepreneurship, skill development, technology, sports and the future of Uttarakhand with young participants.During the interaction, participants raised questions related to the development of the state and the country. They also shared their experiences of various government schemes and offered suggestions on employment, self-employment and access to better opportunities in Uttarakhand.Nabin said that under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership, the potential of India’s youth was being given a new direction while new opportunities were being created for them. He said initiatives such as Digital India, Startup India, Skill India, Make in India and Khelo India had provided young people with platforms to advance according to their talent, capabilities and skills. He added that young people were not merely seeking employment but were also emerging as creators of jobs and new opportunities.He said the role of youth was increasing amid a rapidly changing economy and advances in technology.According to him, new avenues had opened up in areas such as artificial intelligence, startups, innovation, digital technology and entrepreneurship. He said Uttarakhand’s young people had immense talent and potential and that connecting their energy and capabilities with the state’s development could help take Uttarakhand to new heights.He said that in a mountainous state such as Uttarakhand, it was important to expand opportunities in local employment, self-employment, tourism, skill development and entrepreneurship. He added that the ideas, suggestions and aspirations of young people could play an important role in determining the future direction of the state. He called on the youth to turn future challenges into opportunities and actively contribute to building a developed India.He also described social media as a powerful medium and said young people should use it positively for the development of society and the country. He said all 1.4 billion citizens would need to work together to realise the vision of a developed India. He also urged young people to enter politics and public life and contribute to nation-building. He stressed the importance of time management, saying effective use of time was essential for success.Dhami described young people as the country’s greatest strength and said India’s large youth population was providing the nation with new energy, fresh ideas and capabilities. He said the growing use of technology and innovation was also opening up new opportunities for young people.The chief minister said that after assuming office on July 4, 2021, his government began working with the resolve that “the youth and water of the mountains should both serve Uttarakhand.” He said recruitment to vacant posts in government departments was accelerated and that around 34,000 young people had so far been appointed to government services. He also referred to action against irregularities in recruitment examinations, saying members of cheating rackets had been sent to jail and that a crackdown had been launched against those attempting to jeopardize the future of young people.He said the government was not limiting opportunities to government jobs and was also focusing on self-employment, startups and entrepreneurship. He cited the Chief Minister’s Self-Employment Scheme, skill development programmes, homestays and the Chief Minister’s Udyaman Khiladi Scheme as initiatives through which young people were being provided opportunities.The chief minister said Uttarakhand was establishing a new identity in sports and that sports infrastructure was being expanded across the state. He referred to work towards setting up a Sports University in Haldwani and a women’s Sports College in Lohaghat. He also cited Uttarakhand athletes winning more than 100 medals at the National Games, describing it as evidence of the state’s growing sporting talent and changing sports environment.He said opportunities were being created for young people in tourism, local products, science, innovation, artificial intelligence, robotics and other emerging technologies. He also referred to the Investors Summit, saying it had been organized with the objective of generating new investment and employment opportunities, while efforts were under way to expand industrial activity in the mountainous regions of the state.The chief minister said the government was also providing free coaching facilities to young people preparing for competitive examinations to help ensure equal opportunities. He added that the talent, hard work and potential of Uttarakhand’s youth were among the state’s greatest strengths in its effort to build a developed Uttarakhand.BJP state president Mahendra Bhatt, MP Ajay Bhatt, public representatives, party office-bearers and a large number of young people were present at the programme.
Article Summary: BJP national president Nitin Nabin and Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami took part in a youth interaction programme in Haldwani. They discussed careers, employment, entrepreneurship, skill development, technology, sports and the future of the state.

NEW DELHI: The battle for Delhi University Students’ Union (DUSU) is taking shape around an issue that extends beyond the campus gates — where and how thousands of students live — as ABVP filed nominations of seven probable candidates on Thursday and intensified its outreach ahead of the polls.Alok Attri, Ishu Maurya, Lakshya Raj Singh, Nitin Tanwar, Riya Chhawari, Tanya Mavi and Yash Dabas filed nominations, with ABVP set to pick four of them for president, vice-president, secretary and joint secretary after scrutiny.ABVP enters the election defending three of the four central posts it won last year — president, secretary and joint secretary — while NSUI holds the vice-president’s post.But the Satya Niketan PG building tragedy has brought student housing and safety sharply into the election discourse, with rival organisations competing over an issue affecting a large section of DU students dependent on private accommodation.ABVP, which has held protests over the incident, has begun a PG-to-PG survey under its “Aakhir Kab Tak?” campaign to identify fire, structural and basic-facility gaps. It is demanding more affordable university hostels, faster construction of new hostels and stricter safety enforcement in PGs and rented accommodation.The issue, however, is not ABVP’s alone. AISA and SFI, which have renewed their alliance for the election, have also made safe and affordable housing a central plank alongside concessional Metro passes, opposition to fee hikes, public education and academic freedom.ABVP is simultaneously conducting class-to-class outreach and says student feedback will shape its manifesto. It is also pitching the outgoing DUSU’s record, including CCTV cameras, internships, U-Bus services and Pink Booths.ABVP Delhi secretary Sarthak Sharma said the aim was a union that remained “accessible, accountable and responsive throughout the year”.This version gives the report a campus-wide election story rather than an ABVP press-release frame. It also avoids implying that ABVP owns the housing issue when its rivals are making essentially the same concern a major campaign plank.
Article Summary: DUSU polls put student housing and safety in focus after Satya Niketan PG tragedy as ABVP files nominations and rivals make affordable accommodation a key plank. ABVP enters the election defending three of the four central posts it won last year — president, secretary and joint secretary.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) on Friday conducted searches at nine locations in Bihar, Haryana and Delhi in connection with an alleged bank fraud involving Ramnandi Hotels and Resorts Ltd (RHRL), Gaya. The searches were carried out under Section 17 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) at six locations in Gaya, two in Gurugram and one in New Delhi, officials said.RHRL is controlled by Akhouri Gopal and his sons, Nishant and Nitesh, according to officials. The ED action follows an investigation into the alleged diversion of loan funds and suspected attempts to move properties to prevent possible attachment.During the probe, the agency found that RHRL allegedly diverted Rs 58 crore out of the Rs 85 crore disbursed by a consortium of banks led by Central Bank of India. The loans were allegedly obtained on the basis of fake or forged project completion reports provided by the company's chartered accountant.The loan facilities were also backed by personal guarantees from Akhouri Gopal and his family members, officials said.The investigation has also flagged five properties that had been pledged or mortgaged with Tata Motors Ltd against outstanding dues of a related group entity. The properties were allegedly sold recently despite being pledged.According to the ED, the properties were sold at grossly undervalued prices, with the sale deeds showing the consideration as cash receipts. Some of the buyers are suspected to be benamis or proxies of Akhouri Gopal, officials said.The agency suspects the transactions were aimed at alienating the properties and preventing coercive action. Some of the buyers were reportedly people of modest means who may not have had the financial capacity to arrange the amounts involved in the transactions.The proceeds of crime in the case, based on the CBI chargesheet, are estimated at around Rs 131.79 crore, corresponding to the non-performing asset (NPA) value, officials said.The searches are part of the ED's ongoing investigation into the alleged bank fraud and related movement of assets.
Article Summary: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) conducted searches at nine locations in Bihar, Haryana and Delhi in connection with an alleged bank fraud. The searches were carried out under Section 17 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) Some of the buyers are suspected to be benamis or proxies of Akhouri Gopal.

Article Title: Vande row: Do they want Kashmiris in jail? J&K CM Omar Abdullah hits back at Congress
Article Text:
Omar Abdullah

SRINAGAR: Does Congress want more Kashmiris to be jailed?” J&K chief minister Omar Abdullah retorted on Thursday, a day after ally Congress criticised him for the rendition of all six stanzas of Vande Mataram at the inaugural ceremony of International Film Festival of Jammu & Kashmir (IFFJK) on Monday.“It is a statutory obligation. The entire stanza of national song Vande Mataram must be played across the country at the govt events,” the CM said, adding legal action could be taken against those who fail to stand for the full national song.He accused Congress of politicising the issue. “They (Congress) should have stopped this (the law mandating full rendition of the national song) in Parliament. When Congress comes to power, and I pray the Congress comes to power as soon as possible, they can revoke this in Parliament. Let them do it, we have no objection,” Omar told reporters.Congress MP K C Venugopal triggered the war of words on Wednesday, by asking National Conference to “honour the wisdom and judgement of our freedom fighters” and stand with INDIA bloc in singing only the first two stanzas of the national song.
Article Summary: Omar Abdullah accused Congress of politicising the issue. “The entire stanza of national song Vande Mataram must be played across the country at the govt events,” the CM said, adding legal action could be taken against those who fail to stand for the full national song.

Article Title: Brics Summit 2026: Putin to land in Delhi in few hours; Xi arriving Saturday - top developments
Article Text:
India is set to host the two-day BRICS summit in New Delhi, bringing together global leaders while showcasing the country’s cultural heritage.

Key leaders in India

Key agenda, topics in focus

Schedule

India chairs Brics for the fourth time

NEW DELHI: Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov arrived in India ahead of the BRICS Summit 2026.Russian President Vladimir Putin is also scheduled to arrive in India later tonight.The 18th Brics Leaders’ Summit will be held in New Delhi on September 12-13, bringing together leaders of the expanded grouping for discussions on economic cooperation, technology, energy and food security, global governance and major geopolitical issues. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will host the summit at Bharat Mandapam as India concludes its year-long Brics chairship and hold key meetings with Putin, Xi jinping and various other leaders.The summit comes amid looming concerns over Russia-Ukraine war, Middle East crisis, Strait of Hormuz shipping and continuing global trade tensions. Leaders are expected to work towards a New Delhi Declaration, while the two-day programme will also include bilateral meetings, an exhibition visit, a gala dinner and cultural events.Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, South African President Cyril Ramaphosa and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto are among the key leaders expected in New Delhi.UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres will also attend. PM Modi is scheduled to hold bilateral meetings with several leaders on the sidelines of the summit. His meeting with Putin on Friday comes after their recent talks at the SCO summit, while his engagement with Pezeshkian will take place against the backdrop of the Middle East conflict. The Russian president is set to reach in just a few hours with expected time of arrival 1.15am on September 11.The Prime Minister is scheduled to hold bilateral talks with Putin at 3.30 pm and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian at 6.15 pm on Friday. Then, according to sources cited by PTI, PM's meeting with Xi Jinping is scheduled for 6 pm on Saturday. During the Modi-Xi talks, the two leaders are expected to review the situation along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) and discuss further steps to normalise bilateral ties, including expanding trade and investment, people familiar with the matter said.The China leader is scheduled to reach Infdia at 12.25 pm on Saturday, September 12.Also read: Putin meeting PM Modi on Friday; energy, defence high on agenda Xi’s visit is particularly significant as it will be his first trip to India in seven years. The Chinese president is expected to travel with a large delegation, with sources, cited by Reuers, earlier estimating around 400 officials, more than twice the number that accompanied him in 2019. His visit comes as New Delhi and Beijing work to stabilise ties after years of border tensions.Read more: China confirms Xi Jinping's India visit for Brics summit on September 12-13, first trip in 7 years Meanwhile, foreign ministers of Ethiopia and Burundi, Gedion Timothewos and Edouard Bizimana, have already arrived in New Delhi on Thursday. Later, Brazil minister of foreign affairs Mauro Vieira also reached New Delhi. Country's president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will not be coming due to upcoming Brazil elections.Food and energy security, healthcare, disaster resilience and critical supply chains will be among the key areas of discussion.Leaders are also expected to discuss trade, investment, connectivity, cross-border payments, greater use of national currencies, MSME development, digital trade and artificial intelligence.Development finance, climate resilience, expansion of the New Development Bank and reforms of multilateral financial and political institutions are also on the agenda.The Russia-Ukraine war, the Middle East war and concerns over the Strait of Hormuz are expected to feature in discussions on global and regional developments.US tariff policies and wider changes in global trade will provide the broader economic backdrop. Since Brics decisions are consensus-based, differences among members could make negotiations on the joint declaration challenging.New Delhi is gearing up for the two-day summit, with Bharat Mandapam decked up to welcome world leaders.Modi shared a video of the venue on X on Thursday, ending with the message, “India is gearing up for BRICS 2026”. Sharing the video, he wrote: “All set for BRICS 2026!”The video contains visuals of the Bharat Mandapam, the sprawling complex in central Delhi, which has been decked up for the Summit that is being held on September 12-13 under India's chairship.India is hosting the 18th Brics Summit as the grouping's 2026 chair, with leaders of member and partner countries as well as outreach invitees expected to participate.The main leaders’ programme begins on Saturday, September 12.At 2.35 pm, Brics member-country leaders will hold a closed-door session on “Inclusive Global Governance and Strengthening Multilateralism”. At 4.25 pm, leaders will tour the Bharat Innovates Exhibition, followed by a family photograph and joint tree-planting ceremony at 5.05 pm.PM Modi will host a gala dinner at 7.30 pm.Then, on Sunday, September 13, leaders of member countries, partner nations and outreach invitees will begin arriving at 9:55 am. The official group photograph is scheduled for 10.35 am, followed by the main open session at 10:50 am, titled “Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability: Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth”.The summit is expected to conclude with the New Delhi Declaration.The ministry of external affairs expects around 1,200-1,300 journalists to cover the summit, with Indian and foreign media expected to be roughly evenly represented.An International Media Centre is being set up at Bharat Mandapam. The government plans to disseminate information through press releases, websites and social media platforms linked to India’s Brics presidency.Around 160 artistes from India and other Brics countries will perform the “Brics Symphony” at PM Modi’s gala dinner on September 12. The programme will feature Bharatanatyam, Kuchipudi, Odissi and Kathak, along with traditional instruments and vocal performances.A special Brics Friendship Mural is also being created at Bharat Mandapam by artists from member countries, inspired by “Sangam”, or confluence.BRICS banners and posters have gone up across the New Delhi district, while prominent areas including Connaught Place and Khan Market have seen enhanced lighting at night. Security agencies have also stepped up surveillance, with around 500 CCTV cameras deployed across the area, including some equipped with number plate recognition technology.Manish Kumar Agrawal, Special Commissioner of Police (Protective/Security Division), said, "We have made elaborate bandobast by ensuring minimum inconvenience to the public. We have also issued advance advisories regarding traffic arrangements," Agrawal said.Delhi Police has put in place multi-layered security and quick-response arrangements to ensure the movement of visiting leaders and delegates. Senior officers have also been directed to maintain strict vigilance and ensure smooth coordination during the summit.Traffic restrictions are expected in parts of the city during the movement of foreign dignitaries, which could affect commuters despite markets and commercial areas remaining operational.Also read: Going to airport, central Delhi or south Delhi? BRICS traffic restrictions you need to know Connaught Place will remain open from September 11 to 13, although traffic restrictions linked to the summit may affect movement.The Delhi Metro Museum at Supreme Court Metro station will remain closed from September 11 to 13 and reopen on September 15.Rashtrapati Bhavan, the Rashtrapati Bhavan Museum and Amrit Udyan will also remain closed to the public from September 11 to 13. The Change of Guard ceremony scheduled for September 12 will not take place.Also read: Brics Summit, nationwide bank strike tomorrow: Are banks open or shut on September 11? Check details Northern Railway has also made temporary changes to train operations from September 11 to 13. Several trains from New Delhi and nearby stations have been cancelled, diverted, rescheduled or short-terminated/originated during the period. Passengers have been advised to check the National Train Enquiry System (NTES) or call 139 for the latest updates before travelling.Read more: Operations at New Delhi railway station to be regulated; several trains cancelled, diverted - check full list Meanwhile, Delhi is likely to witness rain on both days, with the IMD forecasting light to moderate rainfall in parts of the city, even as temperatures remained above normal on Thursday.India assumed the Brics chairship on January 1, 2026, for the fourth time, after previous chairships in 2012, 2016 and 2021.India’s theme for the year is “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”, with “Humanity First” as its people-centric approach. During its chairship, India has held more than 350 meetings and high-level engagements across more than 25 cities.Brics originally comprised Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa. Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, the UAE and Saudi Arabia joined in 2024, while Indonesia became a member in 2025.Ten countries, including Belarus, Bolivia, Kazakhstan, Cuba, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand, Uganda, Uzbekistan and Vietnam, have joined as partner countries.The 11-member grouping accounts for about 49.5 per cent of the world's population, around 40 per cent of global GDP and about 26 per cent of global trade, according to Indian government figures.
Article Summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, South African President Cyril Ramaphosa and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto are among the key leaders expected in New Delhi. Article Title: Modi-Xi meet: Trade, border on agenda during Xi's 24-hour blitz
Article Text:
Xi Jinping to visit India after 7 years, attend BRICS Summit on Sept 12-13

China announced Thursday President Xi Jinping ’s first visit to India in 7 years, saying he will attend the Brics summit in New Delhi from September 12 to 13 at the invitation of PM Narendra Modi. His bilateral with Modi is scheduled for Saturday evening, according to diplomatic sources.TOI has learnt that Xi will be accompanied by a 67-member government delegation, including political heavyweight and Xi’s right-hand man Cai Qi - member of the standing committee of the CPC Politburo - and foreign minister Wang Yi. A business delegation is arriving separately for the president’s visit that will last exactly for 24 hours, beginning with Xi’s arrival at 12.10 pm on Saturday and 12.20 pm departure the next day.Xi will arrive at Bharat Mandapam around 2 pm on Saturday, where he and other leaders will be welcomed by Modi. The bilateral meeting between the leaders is likely to take place between the Brics closed session on multilateralism and the dinner that Modi will host for the leaders at 7.30 pm in which Xi will also be present.There has been speculation about why Beijing delayed the announcement of the visit, but it’s learnt that China had formally conveyed to the Indian side Xi’s participation weeks earlier.On August 27, China officially requested the Indian embassy in Beijing to issue visas to the president’s delegation.Xi’s visit is expected to reinforce the positive momentum in bilateral ties since the meeting between the leaders on the margins of the BRICS summit in Kazan in 2024, which marked complete disengagement and resolution of issues related to the 2020 eastern Ladakh military standoff. Modi is expected to underline India’s concerns about fair market access, supply chain reliability and balance in bilateral trade in the meeting, as the 2 sides look to boost economic cooperation.The leaders had in Kazan agreed to restart high-level engagements, calling upon Special Representatives on the India-China boundary question to oversee the management of peace and tranquility in border areas, which India calls a prerequisite for overall development of ties, and to explore a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable solution to the boundary question. They also agreed to maintain contact at the level of foreign minister and other senior officials.Since then, the special representatives have thrice held boundary talks, with the latest meeting in August this year resulting in 8 outcomes that included a decision to finalise terms of reference for an early and substantial harvest of boundary delimitation and border management.Modi last year also visited China for the SCO summit, during which he also had a bilateral meeting with Xi. That visit too further solidified the thaw in ties, with both leaders agreeing that India and China are partners, not rivals. Xi’s visit is important for Beijing also as China assumes BRICS presidency next year, succeeding India’s chairship. The president had not travelled to Brazil last year for the BRICS summit.During his visit to Tianjin, Modi had also met Cai and shared his vision for bilateral relations and seeking his support to realise the vision of the two leaders. According to the Indian government, Cai had reiterated the Chinese sides desire to expand bilateral exchanges and further improve relations in line with the consensus reached between the two leaders.
Article Summary: Xi Jinping to visit India after 7 years, attend BRICS Summit on Sept 12-13. His bilateral with Modi is scheduled for Saturday evening, according to diplomatic sources. Xi’s visit is important for Beijing also as China assumes BRICS presidency next year.

Article Title: Tamil Nadu govt tells staff to file annual asset declarations online by October
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

CHENNAI: Tamil Nadu govt has made it mandatory for all govt employees, barring All India Service officers, to submit their annual statements of assets and liabilities online through the Integrated Financial and Human Resources Management System (IFHRMS).The move follows an amendment to Rule 7(3) of Tamil Nadu Government Servants’ Conduct Rules made in Jan 2026 by the DMK regime. Employees are required to declare their immovable properties, including land and buildings, movable assets such as vehicles, jewellery and bank deposits, as well as debts and other liabilities through the IFHRMS portal. “The facility for filing details of assets and liabilities has now been enabled on the IFHRMS portal. The system will make it easier to monitor violations,,” a senior official said.In a recent communication, the govt directed secretaries, heads of departments, district collectors, judges, TNPSC secretary and registrar of Madras high court to instruct employees to file statements for the calendar year ending Dec 31, 2025, by Oct 31, 2026.The date of filing will be recorded in an employee’s ‘annual confidential report’.Failure to submit the statement within the stipulated period will be treated as a violation of the service conduct rules.Employees must file statements of their assets and liabilities as on Dec 31 of each year by March 31 of the succeeding year. The govt has also advised employees to keep their IFHRMS user IDs and passwords secure. Employees have to use Form I for immovable property, Form II for movable property and Form III for debts and other liabilities. After verifying and correcting the details, they must confirm and submit the declaration and download a copy for their records.“Not many employees take the declaration seriously. Submission of the statement will be considered during panel preparation for promotion. Making it mandatory is a welcome step as it would help prevent corruption at all levels,” said a member of Jactto-Geo, an umbrella federation of govt employees.In July, the TVK govt introduced a WhatsApp number — 9498180936 — for reporting instances of govt employees demanding bribes. Heads of departments were directed to ensure that anti-bribery notice boards were prominently displayed in govt offices and public places.
Article Summary: The move follows an amendment to Rule 7(3) of Tamil Nadu Government Servants’ Conduct Rules made in Jan 2026 by the DMK regime. Employees are required to declare their immovable properties, including land and buildings, movable assets such as vehicles, jewellery and bank deposits.

Article Title: BSP's family drama: Why no 'Anand' for Mayawati ahead of Uttar Pradesh elections?
Article Text:
Mayawati said Akash Anand, the BSP's national coordinator, would continue to work in the party. (File Photo)

FIL bends but Mayawati refuses to budge

Akash Anand's on-off jouney with BSP.

Third time unlucky?

Anand's FIL connection and maturity question

Can BSP afford this 'family drama'?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Three promotions. Three demotions. And now staring at a possible exit!Well, that’s how the political scorecard reads for Akash Anand, whose “maturity meter” has not just failed him again, but has also put him on the brink of exit from the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP).7 days after his third demotion, Akash Anand finds himself in a difficult spot, with BSP chief Mayawati opening the doors for his exit from the party. "The people in the party feel that just as he was relieved of all the important responsibilities of the post of national coordinator on September 3, 2026, he should now also be completely freed from the party from today. Therefore, if Akash Anand wants to remain independent in the party, he is free to do so; that is, he has now been completely freed from the party," Mayawati posted on X.This despite the fact that Akash Anand's father-in-law, former Rajya Sabha MP Ashok Siddharth on Thursday bowed before Mayawati's ultimatum and announced his retirement from politics and social life, after the BSP chief linked his "sanyas" to any future reinstatement of responsibilities to her nephew Akash Anand.In an emotional post on X, Siddharth said he was retiring from political and social life "right now", adding that if he ever had to give his life for Mayawati, it would be a matter of pride for him.But neither Siddharth's actions nor his words made any impact on Mayawati.She questioned Siddharth's intentions, saying his "announcement should have come immediately after her call for him to retire." Mayawati alleged that the delay showed that Siddharth's ambitions and intentions had not changed completely."If Ashok Siddharth had even a little genuine concern for the bright future of his son-in-law Akash Anand and the larger interests of the BSP and its Ambedkarite Bahujan movement, he would have announced his retirement without delay," she said.Mayawati also slammed Anand for not reposting her earlier X post linking his future responsibilities in the party to his father-in-law's retirement. She said Anand had earlier reposted posts from her social media account "to demonstrate his loyalty," but had not done so in this case despite the post being in his own interest.Mayawati said this indicated that both Siddharth and Anand were more attached to personal and family interests than to the success of the party and its movement.She questioned whether Anand could effectively serve the BSP while remaining caught between his family ties and the interests of the party."If Akash Anand is less concerned about the real interests of the party and the movement and his own political career, and more attached to family relationships, then it is natural to ask how he can work for the good of the BSP and the movement while remaining double-minded," she said.Akash Anand’s latest demotion was on September 3, when aunt Mayawati announced that her nephew had again lost his political maturity."I have allowed Akash Anand to work in the party, which is before all of you, but Akash Anand still needs to become more mature. Till then, it would not be appropriate to give him a major responsibility in the party," Mayawati said at a national-level meeting of BSP office-bearers.And that ensured Akash Anand, the chief national coordinator of BSP, was back to square one. His Twitter bio reflected the sudden change in his status within the party. From BSP "National Convenor", he became "Party Worker, BSP." Just a few days later, he made yet another edit to his bio, which read: "Party Supporter, BSP." This is how his X bio reads now.It was less than a month back, August 10 to be exact, that Akash Anand had formally launched the BSP’s election campaign for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections from Sadabad assembly constituency in Hathras. He addressed a well-attended rally and launched a broadside against the BJP government in Uttar Pradesh over jobs, education and law and order, while taking digs at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, calling them both “uncle. ”From being anointed Mayawati’s successor to being a party worker and now a party supporter - it has been a tumultuous and bumpy ride for the young Akash Anand. And this time around there is a twist in the tale: Akash’s younger brother Ishan Anand has been brought to the centre stage.On September 3, when Mayawati entered the venue of the meeting of office-bearers, walking behind her was not Akash but his younger brother Ishan. Wearing the BSP's blue sash around his neck, he stood behind his aunt till she settled down.Akash Anand entered politics in 2017 at the young age of 22. Anand, who did his MBA from London, made his political debut with Mayawati at a rally in Uttar Pradesh's Saharanpur, where he shared the dais with Akhilesh Yadav and Ajit Singh.In April 2019, Akash Anand addressed his first rally in Uttar Pradesh's Agra. The BSP was then part of the opposition Mahagathbandhan, an anti-Congress and anti-BJP bloc formed in the run-up to the 2019 general election under the leadership of Akhilesh Yadav and Mayawati with Ajit Singh's Rashtriya Lok Dal.Mayawati appointed him BSP’s national coordinator in June 2019. Since then, it has been a bumpy ride for him. Every promotion since then has been followed by a demotion.After 6 days of suspense, Mayawati finally revealed what triggered her against Akash Anand yet again. In a long post on X, Mayawati explained how Akash Anand had once again, after two years, lost his “political maturity.” And also, what he could do to get it back.The trigger this time around was Ashok Siddharth, the father in law of Akash Anand. Ashok Siddharth was expelled by Maywati from BSP last month for the second time over indiscipline and anti-party stance.Taking to X, the BSP supremo wrote: “It is well known that Ashok Siddharth had previously been expelled for indiscipline and violating guidelines, specifically regarding the distribution of party tickets and a failure to coordinate properly with BSP Maharashtra state president during state elections. He had been reinstated on the condition that he would not repeat such mistakes and would be assigned responsibility of expanding the party's support base only in other states, not in Uttar Pradesh. ”She also informed that Ashok Siddharth will not be taken back into the party “under any circumstances in the future”.Hardening her stand further against Ashok Siddharth, Mayawati stated that a clear path remains for Akash Anand to resume an active leadership role within the movement, provided Siddharth steps aside completely."In such a situation, keeping in mind the interests of the BSP Party and Movement, as well as his own family and the future of his son-in-law Shri Akash Anand, Shri Ashok Siddharth still has the opportunity to renounce his political ambitions, rise above personal interests, etc., and completely retire from politics. Only then will Shri Akash Anand be able to work freely in the party, and only then will the party sympathetically consider restoring his responsibilities so that he can play an active role in the party—this is the general consensus in the party," Mayawati said in her post.Urging people from the Dalit community, to not engage in any action driven by personal or familial interests that creates obstacles in their path, for which “history may not forgive them," Mayawati cited Ashok Siddharth as a prime example of an official prioritising "personal and familial interests and ambitions over the BSP's mission, despite receiving multiple opportunities to reform."The party gave him not just one but several opportunities to mend his ways, but he prioritised his personal and familial interests and ambitions over the BSP's mission, the consequences of which he himself, along with his son-in-law Shri Akash Anand, has had to bear," Mayawati said in her statement.With the UP assembly elections just months away, a family drama is the last thing that the BSP cadres in the state would have hoped for. The party’s trajectory in the state has been downhill. In the 2022 assembly elections, the BSP could win just 1 seat with a vote share of 12.88%. This was a sharp decline from the 19 seats and a 22.23% vote share that Mayawati had got in 2017.The 2024 Lok Sabha elections went on to showcase that Mayawati’s dismal 2022 performance was not an aberration. The BSP supremo failed to win even one Lok Sabha seat, while her party’s vote share dipped to 9.4% from 19.43% in 2019. Clearly, the results reinforced the gradual decline in BSP’s influence among Dalits.From a sweeping majority in 2007 to allegations of being the B-team of BJP, the BSP’s political fortunes have nosedived in the state. The BSP supporters have dwindled and some have even changed loyalties, but what remains still strong is Mayawati’s appeal and popularity among the party’s cadres.However, the 2027 challenge is going to be tough for Maywati and her BSP. The SP-Congress alliance managed to garner a lot of Dalit support in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, upsetting BJP’s applecart in the state and eventually at the Centre. Cleary this was not the time when the BSP chief should have precipitated action against Akash Anand and pitched one nephew against the other.Mayawati needs a strong comeback and to ensure that she has to first set her house in order. All the more, as she has announced that BSP will not enter into any alliance in future elections. The BSP needs to perform if Mayawati wants to remain relevant in the state’s politics. Another poor show where she wins votes but not seats will reinforce allegations that BSP is the B-team of the BJP.
Article Summary: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) national coordinator Akash Anand on brink of exit. BSP chief Mayawati opens doors for his exit from the party. Anand's father-in-law, former Rajya Sabha MP Ashok Siddharth, announces his retirement.

Congress Kerala posted an invented Gujarat street scene; BJP Telangana replied with a fabricated bar scene tagged "Lusiana, Italy", apparently alluding to Sonia Gandhi's birthplace.The '80s came calling, and India's politicians answered with aviators, old albums and a little swagger. Union ports, shipping and waterways minister Sarbananda Sonowal wrote: "80s vibes: Styles fade, but the appeal is forever!" A line fit for a campaign, vintage or otherwise.Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma chimed in: "Back to the 80s eh!" Telangana CM Revanth Reddy appeared beside a motorbike in his post. She shared what she de-scribed as an '80s Savvy magazine cover featuring herself.Union minister Kiren Rijiju followed his AI makeover with a throwback he said needed neither AI nor ChatGPT.Congress MP Shashi Tharoor posted pictures with his sons, Ishaan and Kanishk. "I thought I'd join the trend the old-fashioned way," he wrote, a real photograph a boast of its own amid the trend built on imagining the past.BJP's Tamilisai Soundararajan shared wedding footage featuring then chief minister MGR and opposition leader M Karunanidhi. Rival camps on one guest list.The party accounts added their own gloss. BJP Tamil Nadu's montage of PM Narendra Modi mixed AI styling with archival photographs, ending with "karmayogi". Congress Sevadal posted AI images of Rahul Gandhi.Then came the knowing captions. Congress Kerala's AI image showed a bald man in an Omni van: "A Gujarat street in the 80s." A roadside sign said in Hindi: "Please smile, you are in Delhi." BJP Telangana's bar scene was dated "Circa-1970's". Neither named its target.The clothes belonged to another decade. The urge to have the last word was entirely up to date.
Article Summary: The '80s came calling, and India's politicians answered with aviators, old albums and a little swagger. Then party accounts joined the nostalgia trip, remembering to pack a few jibes for the other side. Congress Kerala posted an invented Gujarat street scene; BJP Telangana replied with a fabricated bar scene.

Article Title: How BJP, Congress turned 80s AI trend turned into an all-out meme war
Article Text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi's original picture from the 80s. Rahul Gandhi's (R) AI-generated image.

What is the trend?

NEW DELHI: What began as another harmless social media trend, turning present-day photographs into portraits straight out of the 1980s, has now found its way into the social feeds of politicians has triggered BJP-Congress war of memes.Over the past few days, Instagram and X have been flooded with AI-generated photographs featuring big hair, aviator sunglasses, denim jackets, vintage suits and the grainy finish of old family albums.BJP leaders were among the first to jump onto the trend. Union commerce minister Piyush Goyal shared an AI-generated photograph of himself dressed in a grey suit and aviators, writing simply: "Vibing to the 80s trend."Union minister Kiren Rijiju followed with his own retro look, posing beside a car in an image designed to resemble a photograph from the decade."Why is everyone going back to the 80s vibes? I'm also forced to 80s nostalgia!" he wrote.Congress Sevadal brought Rahul Gandhi into the picture, posting AI-generated photographs of the leader of opposition with the caption: "Rahul Gandhi catches the 80s trend wave."The BJP's official X handle also shared some original pictures of Prime Minister Narendra Modi believed to be from the 1980s era.What started as politicians recreating their younger selves soon became another format for the BJP and Congress to take veiled potshots at each other with AI doing the set design.The Congress's Kerala unit shared an AI-generated image showing a bald man sitting in the front passenger seat of a Maruti Suzuki Omni, with the caption: "A Gujarat street in the 80s."For context, the van, launched in India in the 1980s, became a familiar sight in Bollywood films where it was often shown being used by goons and kidnappers, eventually earning its own "kidnapping van" meme identity.BJP Gujarat hit back with an AI-generated image of its own.BJP's Telangana unit also responded to the Congress post. It shared an image showing a woman in a red dress dancing on a table inside what appeared to be a bar, with liquor bottles visible in cabinets behind her.The description read: "Lusiana, Italy. Circa-1970s."The BJP did not name anyone in the post either, but the reference was widely seen as an allusion to Lusiana, the Italian town where former Congress president Sonia Gandhi was born.Congress MP Shashi Tharoor , however, found a way of joining the trend without asking AI to take him back in time."The 1980s seem to be back, courtesy of AI. I thought I’d join the trend the old-fashioned way," he wrote, sharing photographs that were actually taken during the decade.The pictures included Tharoor with his sons Ishaan and Kanishk.The trend itself is simple. Users upload a present-day selfie to AI tools such as ChatGPT or Google Gemini and ask them to recreate the image as if it had been taken in the 1980s.Unlike a regular vintage filter, the AI rebuilds the photograph around the person’s face, adding everything from big hairstyles and retro clothes to film grain and old-school studio lighting.The result is a polished throwback image that looks straight out of an old photo album or Bollywood publicity still. The trend has spread rapidly across Instagram and X, with influencers, celebrities and now politicians joining in.
Article Summary: AI-generated images of present-day selfies are being turned into portraits straight out of the 1980s. BJP leaders were among the first to jump onto the trend. The BJP's official X handle also shared some original pictures of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Article Title: Congress-NC rift over Vande Mataram: The ghost of 1987 and ‘big brother’ complex
Article Text:
The 1987 ghost: Vande Mataram row and why Omar Abdullah won't let Congress call the shots in J&K.

Venugopal called on allies to honour the wisdom of the freedom fighters

One alliance, two political vocabularies

Congress and the National Conference have had a stop-start relationship since 1965

The alliance and an unequal power equation

What Omar Abdullah had said in 2024

Statehood: Common demand & source of friction

The Rajya Sabha dispute

We felt that the best chance of winning that seat was with the Congress, and they felt otherwise. So be it. Omar Abdullah on RS seat deadlock

The ghost of 1987

1987: The alliance that became a warning

2009-14: History managed, but not erased

The 1987 ghost & real test of alliance

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The latest Congress-National Conference (NC) clash may have begun with a song, but it is really about something much older: who gets to set the political terms of the alliance in Jammu and Kashmir?CM Omar Abdullah and NC president Farooq Abdullah stood through the full rendition of Vande Mataram on Wednesday at the inaugural International Film Festival in Srinagar. The song was played in its complete six-stanza version, lasting about three minutes and 10 seconds, in line with the Centre's new protocol.This was in sharp contrast with the Congress's stand. Its grand-old party has reaffirmed its 1937 decision to restrict public rendition at party events to the first two stanzas, arguing that the later verses sit uneasily with the pluralist ethos of the freedom movement.Congress general secretary KC Venugopal subsequently said the full version "sits uneasily" with the syncretic and pluralist ethos envisioned by India's freedom fighters and urged allies to stand by the Congress position.The NC was quick to respond, saying the J&K government was only fulfilling its official duty. "After legislative enactment by Parliament, singing Vande Mataram and standing for the song has become a statutory obligation (mandatory legal duty) regardless of the ideological position of any party, group or alliance," said National Conference spokesperson Tanvir Sadiq.A day later, CM Omar Abdullah also defended the move and said the issue had been needlessly politicised."This is not just for Jammu and Kashmir; it applies to the entire country. In states governed by the Congress, the same will happen at government functions," he said."This is now a statutory obligation. Even today, at the closing ceremony, a Union minister will be present. The national anthem will be played there, and the national song will be played too," he added.The Vande Mataram row is the latest in the list of NC-Congress differences that have surfaced post-election. However, in J&K, the dispute carries an additional historical charge.The NC has spent decades constructing its political identity around a particular proposition: New Delhi can be a partner, but it cannot be the political proprietor of Kashmir's choices.That is where the ghost of 1987 enters.The Vande Mataram dispute has once again exposed an asymmetry that has repeatedly surfaced between the two parties.Congress has to balance its position across India. For Abdullahs' NC, the principal political constituency remains rooted in J&K, where questions of identity, autonomy, federalism and the relationship with New Delhi carry a much more immediate electoral meaning.It is also why the latest row is not an isolated irritant in the alliance.In December 2025, for instance, Omar Abdullah explicitly distanced the NC from Congress's "vote chori" campaign, saying Congress was free to choose its own agenda but that it was not automatically the agenda of the INDIA bloc. With this, Omar tried to assert his party's political autonomy within the alliance.And that has been the recurring pattern.The 2024 assembly election gave the NC-Congress relationship a new lease of life, but it also made the asymmetry between the two parties stark.The alliance crossed the majority mark with 49 seats, with the NC winning 42, Congress six and CPM one. The BJP emerged with 29, PDP three and independents seven.The pre-poll negotiations themselves had not been effortless: the parties agreed that NC would contest 51 seats and Congress 32, while several constituencies remained "friendly contests".The campaign also revealed the limits of joint ownership. Congress and NC leaders did not always campaign together. In Sopore, where the two allies were in a friendly contest, Rahul Gandhi and Omar Abdullah campaigned for their respective candidates separately.During the campaign, Omar Abdullah had publicly noted that Rahul Gandhi should dedicate more campaign time and effort to the Jammu region in addition to Kashmir to maximise electoral impact.Omar himself gave the practical reason for the alliance during the campaign: it was intended to prevent a hung assembly and give voters an alternative.The alliance won the election, and the next question was: what does each side get to claim as its own?The first major post-election rupture came even before the new government had settled in.Omar Abdullah became CM in October 2024, but Congress chose to stay out of his ministry, citing restoration of statehood as its priority. While Congress backed the NC government from outside, its absence highlighted a strategic divide within the alliance. Omar had to engage with Delhi to govern the Union Territory, while Congress sought to pressure the Centre from outside. That difference in approach has repeatedly resurfaced.In July 2025, Congress announced protests in Jammu, Srinagar and Delhi and Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge wrote to PM Narendra Modi seeking legislation to restore J&K's statehood. The NC leadership was irritated because the announcement had not been coordinated with the ruling party. Some NC leaders described Congress's campaign as counterproductive and even as "sabotage" of the government's own efforts.Omar's objection was that Congress had launched the campaign without informing or consulting the NC, leaving its alliance partner caught off guard.The difference is clearer on Article 370 . The NC's 2024 manifesto explicitly called for the restoration of Articles 370 and 35A and reversal of the changes made after August 2019. Congress has similarly opposed the 2019 constitutional changes, but in its recent campaigns placed greater emphasis on the restoration of statehood.Omar reiterated in the J&K assembly in February that his government remained committed to restoring special status, even as statehood remained an immediate demand. By July 2026, he was also linking the restoration of statehood to any future discussion on J&K's earlier constitutional position.This has given the two parties different political priorities.In October 2025, the disagreement moved from ideology to seats. J&K was electing four Rajya Sabha members. The NC, which had emerged as the dominant party in the assembly, initially discussed leaving one seat for Congress.Talks failed.The NC eventually fielded candidates for all four seats after Congress decided not to contest the fourth seat it had been offered, arguing that it was not among the "safe seats" it had sought.Omar's response was strikingly matter-of-fact: "So be it."The NC-Congress disagreement ultimately cost the alliance a clean sweep, with the BJP winning the fourth seat Congress had declined to contest.To understand why the NC may be particularly sensitive to questions of control, one has to go back not merely to 1987 but to 1984.Farooq Abdullah's government was dismissed on July 2, 1984, after 12 NC legislators defected. Ghulam Mohammad Shah, Farooq's brother-in-law and leader of the defecting group, formed the government with Congress support. Contemporary accounts described the episode as a central-government intervention in Kashmir politics; Farooq called the dismissal unconstitutional.For the NC, this was not an abstract constitutional episode. It was a direct lesson in the vulnerability of a regional government to New Delhi's political machinery.Then came 1986.Rajiv Gandhi and Farooq Abdullah reached an agreement that brought the two parties together electorally. A Human Rights Watch report noted that the accord deepened a sense of betrayal among many Kashmiris, who saw Farooq Abdullah compromising with the same Congress party that had pushed him out of office two years earlier.The NC-Congress alliance won 66 of J&K's 76 assembly seats in 1987. But the result was overshadowed by the emergence of the Muslim United Front as an opposition platform, arrests of its candidates and workers, and widespread allegations of electoral rigging. Human Rights Watch later described the election as a turning point that contributed to widespread disillusionment with electoral politics.The significance of 1987 for the NC, therefore, is about the political memory it created. A generation of Kashmiri activists came to believe that the democratic route had been closed to them, a perception that became part of the backdrop to the insurgency that followed.The episode also left an enduring paradox. Congress was simultaneously the NC's electoral partner and a major force at the Centre. That history helps explain the NC's instinct to work with Congress while resisting any perception that Delhi is dictating its regional agenda.That distrust predates the 1980s. In 1953, Sheikh Abdullah was dismissed and arrested after his relationship with the Union government deteriorated. The circumstances were very different, but the political memory was similar: central intervention could reshape J&K's politics. For the NC, unlike many other regional parties, Congress's centralising past is therefore not distant history but part of its own political inheritance.The two parties showed they could overcome that history after the 2008 assembly election. The NC won 28 seats and Congress 17, and the parties formed a coalition government with Omar Abdullah as CM in 2009.But the partnership remained contested. Differences over AFSPA, administrative issues and governance repeatedly surfaced. In 2011, Congress called for consensus on AFSPA while Omar maintained that the state government was an important stakeholder.By 2014, the alliance had run its course and Congress chose to contest the assembly election separately. NC leaders argued that the association with a centrist national party had diluted the party's pro-Valley credentials, with one senior NC leader calling Congress a "very bad alliance partner".While 1987 may still shape the NC's political instincts, it would be too simplistic to link every present-day disagreement to that history. The political and constitutional context has changed; however, the experience remains part of the backdrop to the relationship.The lesson for the NC, as we saw in the last election, has not been to avoid Congress, but to work with it where interests converge while retaining its own political space.The Vande Mataram dispute, therefore, is less significant in itself than what it reveals about continuing differences over statehood, Article 370, seat-sharing and the balance between Congress's national strategy and the NC's regional politics.The alliance can survive such differences, but the interesting question now is how durable it will be, which willdepend on how well the two parties manage their competing political priorities.
Article Summary: Congress and the National Conference have had a stop-start relationship since 1965. Omar Abdullah and Farooq Abdullah stood through the full rendition of Vande Mataram at the inaugural International Film Festival in Srinagar. The song was played in its complete six-stanza version, lasting about three minutes and 10 seconds, in line with the Centre's new protocol. This was in sharp contrast with the Congress's stand.

Article Title: 2.5 lakh crore spent on disaster management in 11 years: Amit Shah
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Around Rs 2.5 lakh crore has been spent in the disaster management sector over the last 11 years, increasing allocations for national and state disaster response funds manifold, home minister Amit Shah said while chairing the third meeting of the governing body of National Institute of Disaster Management (NIDM) Thursday.Shah said the process of creating digital disaster databases at national and state levels has begun, an obligation for all UN member states as decided in Sendai framework in 2015. "Disasters were viewed only from the perspective of relief and rehabilitation. Today, we have entered a new era based on three pillars - risk reduction, early warning systems and 'zero casualty'."The minister said that "allocation towards the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) has increased nearly fourfold, while the allocation under the NDRF has increased nearly threefold". In addition, the 16th Finance Commission has also provided for Rs 2 lakh crore. He said the agriculture department should focus on permanent preparedness to deal with locust swarm attacks originating from the Pakistan side.
Article Summary: Around Rs 2.5 lakh crore has been spent in the disaster management sector over the last 11 years. Home minister Amit Shah said the process of creating digital disaster databases at national and state levels has begun. He said agriculture department should focus on permanent preparedness to deal with locust swarm attacks originating from the Pakistan side.

Article Title: Global climate record: August this year joint-warmest month with July '23
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Aug 2026 was the joint-warmest month ever recorded globally across all calendar months, on a par with July 2023, said Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) of the European Union's space programme on Thursday.It noted that this Aug was 1.65° Celsius above the estimated pre-industrial (1850-1900) baseline, marking the first month above 1.5° Celsius since Nov 2025, and the period from June to Aug 2026 was the joint-warmest three-month period on record globally, on a par with 2024."Aug 2026 was a remarkable month in the global climate record. It was both the warmest Aug and the warmest month ever recorded," said Samantha Burgess, strategic lead for climate at European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts. Though the global average temperature rise in the month breached the limit of 1.5°C, it technically did not cross the Paris Agreement threshold, which actually refers to long-term temperature increase over decades, not over one to five years.Under the Paris Agreement, countries agreed to keep long-term global average surface temperature well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels and pursue efforts to limit it to 1.5°C by end of century.Nevertheless, the rise in temperatures to this level in Aug is a stark warning that the world is getting warmer, with its consequences of extreme weather events, glacier melt, sea-level rise and uneven distribution of rainfall over a short period of time being visible across the globe."Until humanity stops burning colossal amount of coal, oil and gas, the pollution this causes will keep baking our planet, and extreme heat will keep smashing all-time records, killing millions and costing trillions, hitting transport and health systems, and pushing up prices for household basics like food," said UN Climate Change executive secretary Simon Stiell in his response to the report.Aug in India was the warmest Aug in the country since 1901, with a mean monthly temperature of 28.01°C.
Article Summary: Aug 2026 was the joint-warmest month ever recorded globally across all calendar months. This Aug was 1.65° Celsius above the estimated pre-industrial (1850-1900) baseline. It was the first month above 1.5° Celsius since Nov 2025.

Article Title: Last year's row in mind, govt says won't reduce med PG cut-off
Article Text:
