NEW DELHI: After facing severe backlash last year for reducing the cut-off percentile to zero for admission to medical colleges for super speciality courses, the Centre Thursday told Supreme Court that it has decided not to reduce cut-off marks this year, but the top court asked govt to take a fresh look and reconsider its decision.Additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati told a bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe about govt's decision. She informed the court that the decision was arrived at after consultations between all stakeholders - ministry of health, medical counselling committee (MCC) and National Medical Commission (NMC)."As per the directions of Supreme Court in the Kevin Joy case (2023), it has been decided to conduct a 'special stray round' by the medical counselling committee for the purpose of filling up the vacant super speciality seats arising out of NEET-SS 2025 counselling without reduction in the percentile criteria prescribed for admission in the said special stray round," Bhati said while placing before the court a one-page note on govt's decision.Advocate Rashmi Nandakumar, appearing for some of the petitioners, however, told the bench that around 2,000 seats in colleges would remain vacant if the cut-off percentile was not reduced. She said the authorities have consistently adopted appropriate measures, including special rounds, mop-up rounds, stray vacancy rounds and relaxation of eligibility criteria, whenever substantial super speciality seats remained vacant to ensure optimum utilisation of available seats.Taking note that a substantial number of seats would get wasted, the bench asked the Centre to reconsider its decision and brief the court on the next date of hearing. As the ASG urged the court to put it in its order, the bench passed a brief order on reconsideration of the decision. The petitioners pleaded that at least a mop-up/stray vacancy round be conducted for seats remaining vacant after completion of the ongoing counselling process so that no super speciality seat was allowed to go to waste.With over 18,000 post-graduate medical seats across the country remaining vacant, the National Board of Examination in Medical Sciences (NBEMS) revised the qualifying percentile for NEET-PG 2025 admissions, reducing it to zero from the 40th percentile for reserved categories -- which enabled even those scoring as low as minus 40 out of 800 to take part in the third round of counselling for PG medical seats. According to the notice published by NBEMS, the NEET-PG cut-off for the general category was reduced to the seventh percentile from the 50th.
Article Summary: The Centre told Supreme Court that it has decided not to reduce cut-off marks this year. The top court asked govt to take a fresh look and reconsider its decision. With over 18,000 post-graduate medical seats across the country remaining vacant, the National Board of Examination in Medical Sciences revised qualifying percentile for NEET-PG 2025 admissions.

Article Title: SC junks anti-HPV vax PIL, says plea has ulterior motive
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday dismissed a PIL by a doctors' association challenging India's nationwide human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination programme for adolescent girls to protect them against cervical cancer and said it did not behove medical practitioners to take an anti-vaccine stance.Though the NGO's counsel clarified at the outset that the PIL was not against the vaccination programme but for putting in place mechanisms to take care of adverse reactions and compensation, a bench led by CJI Surya Kant said, "The PIL is definitely anti-vaccine." It gave the option to the lawyer to withdraw or invite adverse comments.When the counsel continued to argue for prior informed consent of parents of the target population of adolescent girls, the bench said the PIL appeared to have been filed with an ulterior motive and lacked bona fide. It said when there was an established mechanism for taking care of adverse reactions and compensation in individual cases, it did not behove doctors to oppose vaccination when World Health Organisation had recommended it.The NGO said eminent oncologists have pointed to data that shows cervical cancer incidence has declined over the past three decades.
Article Summary: Supreme Court dismisses a PIL by a doctors' association challenging India's vaccination programme for adolescent girls to protect them against cervical cancer. A bench led by CJI Surya Kant said, "The PIL is definitely anti-vaccine" It gave the option to the lawyer to withdraw or invite adverse comments.

Article Title: Modi to meet Iran prez today amid efforts to bridge the ‘gulf’

NEW DELHI: For the first time in 8 years, an Iranian president will visit India with Masoud Pezeshkian set to arrive in New Delhi for the 18th BRICS summit on Friday, amid escalating West Asia tensions that have cast a shadow over the summit. Shortly after his arrival, Pezeshkian will participate in the BRICS Business Forum meeting along with PM Narendra Modi, Russian President Vladimir Putin and other leaders before joining Modi for a bilateral in the evening.The last Iranian president to visit India was Hassan Rouhani in 2018. While Iran has confirmed participation by the president in the BRICS summit, Saudi Arabia and the UAE - both parties to the West Asia conflict along with Tehran - will be represented by foreign minister Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud and Abu Dhabi crown prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan respectively.Pezeshkian is likely to reiterate his message before Modi for India to help end the war and suitably address Tehran's concerns related to the current situation, including through a strong condemnation of "illegal aggression" against Iran, in the proposed BRICS declaration. In his meetings with both Putin and Pezeshkian on Friday, Modi is expected to stress the need for new members to subscribe to consensus in the grouping on critical issues and work together for a unified joint declaration.India agreed to the recent SCO Bishkek Declaration that condemned attacks on Iran. The declaration did not name the US or Israel though to prevent any resistance from members that have also cultivated ties with Washington.However, with the presence of UAE in BRICS, balancing the interests of both sides has not been easy for India’s BRICS chairship. It’s unlikely that the UAE will agree to an SCO-like formulation without seeking an explicit condemnation of Iranian attacks.Gulf states like the UAE and Saudi Arabia are only dialogue partners in SCO.India will prioritise the UN Charter, dialogue and diplomacy, freedom of navigation and civilian protection in the declaration. If the deadlock persists, the government will look to insulate economic agreements from the West Asia discord by acknowledging respective national positions.The BRICS foreign ministers’ meeting earlier this year ended without a consensual statement, with Tehran adamant on a condemnation of the alleged violation of international law by the US and Israel and accusing the UAE of being directly involved in aggression against Iran.
Article Summary: Masoud Pezeshkian set to arrive in New Delhi for the 18th BRICS summit on Friday. The last Iranian president to visit India was Hassan Rouhani in 2018. Saudi Arabia and the UAE - both parties to the West Asia conflict along with Tehran - will be represented by foreign minister and crown prince respectively.

New Delhi: Having secured nearly 2,000 convictions in food safety cases across the country, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) is now stepping up enforcement, including holding e-commerce platforms responsible for products sold through them and proposing stricter action against high-fat, sugar and salt (HFSS) foods near schools, its CEO Rajit Punhani said Thursday.FSSAI will begin checks on e-commerce platforms from next month. Article Title: Need social media firewalls, safeguards for minors: Supreme Court

NEW DELHI: With minors' access to social media platforms banned in many countries, Supreme Court Thursday took the first step in this regard by seeking govt's response to a PIL that said opening a social media account is akin to signing a contract - which is impermissible for a person below 18 years of age under Indian law.The plea by senior advocate H S Phoolka, on behalf of NGO Just Rights for Children Association, found resonance with a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, which said there was a need for safeguards and firewalls to protect minors.Phoolka said children were at present permitted to independently create and maintain accounts on social media platforms and access digital platforms "notwithstanding their statutory incapacity to enter into a contract under Section 11 of Indian Contract Act, 1872", and said such contracts are void ab initio.The NGO said the absence of an effective and uniform mechanism giving practical effect to such statutory incapacity in the digital environment exposed children to "foreseeable risks, including online grooming, sexual exploitation, trafficking, behavioural profiling, misuse of personal data, cyberbullying, exposure to age-inappropriate content and other harms affecting their safety, dignity, development and well-being".It requested the court to direct govt to ensure that persons below 18 years of age are not permitted to enter into contracts with digital platforms, including social media, online gaming, content-sharing, live-streaming and other user generated content platforms. It said minors could be permitted to access lawful, educational and age-appropriate digital content through accounts maintained and controlled by their parents or guardians, subject to an appropriate regulatory framework.Phoolka said social media platforms applied US law in India, not Indian law. In US, a person above 13 years can lawfully enter into a contract. CJI Kant said, "We need some safeguards in India." Justice Bagchi said, "There should be some firewalls."The NGO said opening of accounts includes acceptance of contractual terms and conditions, user agreements, privacy policy, etc, which govern the relationship between the platform and the user.Referring to provisions of Digital Personal Data Protection Act, the NGO said Section 9 required verifiable parental or guardian consent for processing a child's personal data. The Act also imposes restrictions concerning detrimental processing, tracking, behavioural monitoring and targeted advertising, it said.However, the existing statutory framework does not expressly prohibit a person below 18 from independently creating an account on a digital platform nor does it prescribe a uniform mechanism for preventing such independent opening of accounts, it said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court seeks govt's response to a PIL that said opening a social media account is akin to signing a contract. The plea by senior advocate H S Phoolka found resonance with a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana.

Article Title: Chandrayaan-2 orbiter is still alive and helping in subsequent future lunar missions: Sr Indian scientist
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: A senior Indian space scientist on Thursday said that the orbiter of the Chandrayaan-2 mission, which was said to be a failed mission after its lander crashlanded on the south pole region of Moon, is still alive and is helping in planning and executing subsequent Indian lunar missions.During the AEDEX conference at Yashobhoomi here on Thursday, Anil Bhardwaj, director of Ahmedabad-based Physical Research Laboratory (PRL) under the Department of Space, said, “It was the Chandrayaan-2 orbiter that provided crucial information to Isro about where to land the Chandrayaan-3 lander.”Chandrayaan-2 orbiter, which was launched in 2019, is currently operating from the Moon’s orbit. “It has the highest resolution among all the assets in the world operating on the Moon. It is now being used for future missions,” Bhardwaj said.Chandrayaan-2 orbiter carried eight scientific payloads designed to study the lunar surface, minerals, and exosphere. The orbiter is equipped with the Orbiter High Resolution Camera (OHRC), which features a spatial resolution of about 0.25 meters (25 cm) to 0.32 meters per pixel from a 100-kilometer lunar orbit.“For Chandrayaan-4, we have built sensors that will help in landing and bringing back lunar samples back to Earth,” the PRL director said.“Chandrayaan-5 will be a joint mission with Japan agency JAXA, where the lander will try to land in the permanently-shadowed region of the Moon. This region is near the south pole of the Moon and it never sees the sunlight. This will be a very challenging mission. The rover will go inside the permanently-shadowed region and explore for the first time the area. There again we are trying to put up very unique sensors to provide us information about the distribution of water.So sensor development is happening at a speedy level.”“India is also working on hi-tech sensors for in-situ (natural place) experiments,” Bhardwaj said. He also said the work is on in developing a heating system so that the lander can survive freezing temperatures during the 14 Earth nights (one lunar night is equal to 14 Earth days).
Article Summary: Chandrayaan-2 orbiter, which was launched in 2019, is currently operating from the Moon’s orbit. “It has the highest resolution among all the assets in the world operating on the Moon. It is now being used for future missions,” Anil Bhardwaj said.

CHENNAI/NEW DELHI: As about 1,800 of the more than 4,000 super-specialty medical seats are lying vacant even after two rounds of counselling, Supreme Court on Thursday asked the Union govt to consider lowering the NEET-SS 2025 qualifying cutoff marks.“Having examined the matter from different perspectives, we are of the opinion that it may be necessary to reconsider the decision for reducing the cut-off percentile,” a bench of Justice Pamidighantam Sri Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe said.“This is rather compelling because a large number of seats have remained unfilled even as of today,” the court said in the case concerning admissions under NEET-SS 2025 counselling.The bench asked additional solicitor-general Aishwarya Bhati to convey its concern to the Union health ministry and seek an appropriate decision and listed the matter for Sept 17.Earlier, Centre told Supreme Court that it had decided not to reduce the cut-off marks this year after consultations between all stakeholders — ministry of health, medical counselling committee (MCC) and National Medical Commission (NMC).“As per the directions of Supreme Court in the Kevin Joy case (2023), it has been decided to conduct a ‘special stray round’ by the medical counselling committee for the purpose of filling the vacant super-specialty seats arising out of NEET-SS 2025 counselling without reduction in the percentile criteria prescribed for admission in the said special stray round,” Bhati said, placing before the court a one-page note on the govt’s decision.Advocate Rashmi Nandakumar, appearing for some of the petitioners, however, told the bench that around 2,000 seats in colleges would remain vacant if the cut-off percentile was not reduced. She said that in the past, authorities had conducted special rounds, mop-up rounds, stray vacancy rounds and relaxation of eligibility criteria, whenever substantial super-specialty seats remained vacant. She said that at least a mop-up/stray vacancy round be conducted for seats remaining vacant after completion of the ongoing counselling process so that no super-specialty seat would go waste.Senior counsel P Wilson, who appeared on behalf of service doctors in Tamil Nadu, told the court that the 1,800 super-specialty seats remaining vacant included cardiology, neurosurgery and oncology — disciplines that train doctors to manage some of the country’s most complex illnesses. Allowing such seats to lapse would waste public investment and deepen the shortage of trained specialists, he said.Doctors told TOI that they were tired of waiting for admissions. The eligibility test for super-specialty admissions was completed in Dec 2025, and results were announced a month later. Until now, two rounds of counselling have been completed, and more than 1,800 seats, including those in cardiology, cardiothoracic surgery, neurosurgery, and haematology, are vacant. “How can so many doctors, physicians and surgeons, be kept on wait for such a long time?” asked Dr R Sathish, a physician.“Unlike in MBBS or sometimes PGs, most candidates are breadwinners. Admissions to a super-specialty course means training while working for a hospital. Many have quit jobs in Feb waiting for admissions. While the seat we want is vacant, we don’t get it,” he said.Experts said that in earlier years, the authorities reduced the qualifying cutoff to zero after regular counselling rounds. “That made doctors who had appeared for the examination eligible to compete for vacant seats. Those single digits, zero or negative marks, become eligible,” said Dr K Senthil, former member of the postgraduate board of National Medical Commission. This relaxation offers an immediate way to prevent seats from going unused, without addressing broader issues such as weak job prospects after training, modest salaries, demanding work conditions and uncertain career paths, he said.
Article Summary: About 1,800 of the more than 4,000 super-specialty medical seats are lying vacant. Supreme Court on Thursday asked the Union govt to consider lowering the NEET-SS 2025 qualifying cutoff marks. Centre told Supreme Court that it had decided not to reduce the cut-off marks this year.

As orbits become more crowded, technologies more powerful, and actors more numerous, our choices must be clear: cooperation over confrontation; sustainability over short-term gain; and inclusion over exclusion," he said.Sending a global message from the summit, Modi said, “We will explore together, innovate together and protect space together, for all humanity, and for generations to come.”

Article Title: Brics turns 25: How a Goldman Sachs acronym became a global power bloc
Article Text:
New Delhi will play host to the 18th Brics Summit

From a Wall Street acronym to a global grouping

Why Brics matters in the changing global order

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The 18th Brics Summit is set to take place in New Delhi on September 12-13, bringing together leaders of the expanded grouping at a time when wars, trade tensions and a shifting global order are testing its ability to act as a united bloc.India is hosting the summit as the current Brics chair, with the grouping now comprising 11 members and 10 partner countries.Under the theme “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability,” New Delhi has placed greater focus on cooperation across economic and financial issues, technology, energy, development and global governance.The scale of that transformation becomes clearer when traced back to the origins of Brics, a term coined 25 years ago by a Goldman Sachs economist to describe four emerging economies that he believed would become major drivers of global growth.Twenty-five years ago, Brics did not exist as a political grouping. It was a term coined by Goldman Sachs economist Jim O’Neill in 2001 to describe Brazil, Russia, India and China as emerging economies that could become major drivers of global growth.His paper, Building Better Global Economic BRICs, argued that the weight of these economies in the world economy would rise significantly and called for their greater representation in global policymaking forums.The transition from an economic concept to a government-led grouping began in 2006, when the foreign ministers of Brazil, Russia, India and China met on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York. The first summit of their leaders followed in 2009 in Yekaterinburg, Russia, giving the grouping a formal leaders-level platform.The following year, South Africa joined, turning BRIC into Brics and giving the grouping its first member from Africa.The next major transformation came at the 2023 Johannesburg Summit, when Brics agreed to its first large-scale expansion. Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia and the UAE were invited to join from January 1, 2024. Indonesia subsequently became the bloc's 11th full member in January 2025.The expansion also created a partner-country category, allowing a wider group of developing economies to engage with Brics without becoming full members.Brics has evolved from a forum focused largely on economic cooperation into a broader platform for emerging and developing economies seeking a greater role in global governance.Its members have repeatedly called for reforms in institutions such as the United Nations and international financial institutions, arguing that the architecture of global governance should better reflect the changing balance of economic power.Its growing importance is also backed by institutions created by the grouping itself. The New Development Bank, established in 2015, was designed to mobilise resources for infrastructure and sustainable-development projects in Brics and other emerging and developing economies.The bloc's significance has increased further with its expansion. The addition of countries such as Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, the UAE and Indonesia has widened Brics' economic and geographic reach and strengthened its claim to be a platform for the Global South.
Article Summary: The 18th Brics Summit is set to take place in New Delhi on September 12-13. India is hosting the summit as the current Brics chair. The grouping now comprises 11 members and 10 partner countries. Brics has evolved from a forum focused on economic cooperation into a broader platform for emerging and developing economies seeking a greater role in global governance.
